title: Mighty One, Whose Name Is Holy
description: Mighty One, Whose Name Is Holy in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Pierpont wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 414, “For a Charitable Occasion”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Might-y One, whose name is ho-ly, Thou wilt save Thy work a-live, And the spir-it of the low-ly Thou wilt vis-it and re-vive. What Thy pro-phets thus have spo-ken, A-ges wit-ness as they roll; Bleed-ing hearts and spi-rits bro-ken, Touched by Thee, O God, are whole.

lines: Mighty One, whose name is holy,
Thou wilt save Thy work alive,
And the spirit of the lowly
What Thy prophets thus have spoken,
Touched by Thee, O God, are whole.
And through night's cold vault descending,
Loosed from chains Thy servant Paul.
Father, as Thy love is endless,
Deign to visit, e'en by us;
So shall each, with spirit fervent
Where there's neither want nor woe.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Pierpont died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Pierpont (1785–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
